claims.text: The proposed material is a W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr refractory high-entropy alloy coating.
Approximately 10-15 at.% Cr is the controlled range that will optimize the W-V-Ta-Ti alloy.
The W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr coating can be fabricated by laser cladding on 42-CrMo steel.
The alloy feedstock is in powder form.
The W-V-Ta-Ti matrix has a tendency to form brittle Laves phases or non-protective oxides.
A laser linear energy density above or at 2.83 J/mm is required to obtain a single BCC phase and suppress segregation or Laves-phase formation.
Processing in argon prevents elemental segregation and helps ensure a single BCC solid solution.
Rapid solidification and Cr-induced lattice distortion suppress formation of brittle C14 Laves phase.
Cr addition produces a dense, continuous, protective Cr2O3 surface scale in this alloy.
The Cr2O3 scale improves oxidation resistance by acting as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The high cooling rate of laser cladding stabilizes a single BCC solid solution in W-V-Ta-Ti-Cr and prevents Laves-phase precipitation.
The coating will have significantly greater microhardness than the 42-CrMo substrate because of solid-solution strengthening and its BCC structure.
The Cr-containing coating will reduce the parabolic oxidation-rate constant by more than 30% relative to uncoated steel or a Cr-free RHEA.
The coating will show no observable oxide-scale spallation after 100 hours at 900-1000 degrees Celsius.
Uncoated 42-CrMo steel or Cr-free W-V-Ta-Ti forms non-protective WO3 or V2O5 and consequently undergoes rapid oxidation and lower elevated-temperature hardness.
Cr must exceed a minimum amount needed for a continuous chromia scale but remain below an amount that induces excessive brittle-phase formation.
The cited same-system study varies Cr content but does not establish 10-15 at.% as the definitive optimum.
Refractory high-entropy alloys containing elements such as Ti, V, Ta, Cr, and W generally exhibit high melting temperature, hardness, thermal stability, and resistance to high-temperature softening.
The proposed coating is suitable for oxidation testing in air at temperatures up to 1000 degrees Celsius.

contradictions.description: The initial state calls W-V-Ta-Ti a quinary alloy even though only four elements are named; the fifth element Cr is described elsewhere as the subsequent addition.
The energy boundary alternates between strictly greater than 2.83 J/mm and at least 2.83 J/mm. The experiment includes exactly 2.83 J/mm, which satisfies the latter but not the former.

The boundary sentence grammatically states that the hypothesis can hold if the laser energy density is insufficient, whereas the intervention and conditions state that sufficient energy density is required to maintain the BCC phase.
